Pope led the way for the first few miles but later Presland and Hyde fought the race out in very determined fashion.

McMullen, Hyde, Pope, Scammel, Green, Fletcher and Holland, were the most prominent. The race proceeded with the first position undecided and not until two miles from home could Green, Pope and Hyde shake off the others.
Len Fletcher was in good form and finished second to Hyde, after a tremendous struggle with Pope, of Woodford Green A.C. We finished six men in the first sixteen—excellent team work.

The same course as last year was used and Hyde, Fletcher and Pope took the lead in turn. They were still together with Fletcher, if anything, a yard in front, when Hyde suffered disqualification for the second year in succession.
Had he returned this time in the former race he would have been placed 4th, after Fletcher, Pope and Tommy Green. Moreover, his time was 1¾ min. faster than Frank Elson's when winning last year.

The programme also included a 2 miles Team Walk to which we received an invitation, together with Woodford Green A.C., Enfield A.C., Highgate H., Surrey A.C. and the promoting club, Polytechnic H., Hyde, of Enfield, won, followed by Cooper and Pope, of Woodford Green, and Fletcher, of our Club.

Pope in action on the Battersea Park Track. As usual, the competition consisted of races at 5, 3, 2 and 1 Miles, with two men from each of the competing clubs contesting each event, no walker being allowed to turn out at more than one distance.

Pope, of Woodford Green A.C. upon his recent performances in creating six new World's walking records at the White City Track. We, who struggle round the track with difficulty can appreciate better than anyone the merit of the new figures.

The first event was the five miles race, and in this Pope, the World's Hour Record holder (Woodford Green A.C.); Redman (Metropolitan A.C.) and Richardson (Woodford Green A.C.), both ex-Junior winners, and Archilbald, who has many fine performances to his credit, soon dropped the rest of the field.

He was well outside Pope's figures at five miles, but continued for 9¼ miles, when he retired an obviously tired man. Perhaps the early start was not conducive to fast short-distance track work, and the lack of suitable opposition must have affected him adversely.

Pope, Fletcher and Wright preferred to start comparatively slowly, and speed up as the race progressed. Churcher walked strongly throughout and dropping his opponents, won fairly easily from Bidgood and Bentley, who were to fight out the Police Long Distance Championship on the following Thursday.
Jack Bidgood was instructed to get Pope and Kent of Woodford, and like the good worker and team man that he is, he duly carried out his instructions.
McMullen, Hyde, Pope, Scammell, Green, Fletcher and Holland were the most prominent. Our 'A' team packed in fine fashion to win the scratch team race (3,6,7,9).
